method: Original SHA-256 verification, atomscan --no-update --mode slow, cleave facts, Rizin and independent Capstone path/call review, pefile structure parsing, isolated Unicorn byte reconstruction with intercepted APIs. No native sample or remote payload was executed; no malware endpoint was fetched.

samples.identity: Node-carried macOS credential stealer and local wallet replacer
samples.marker_line: macOS credential stealer: phishes, uploads secrets, replaces wallet
LookFor packed downloader: hidden launch; correct false trait claims

samples.identity: StormAttack persistence/DLL injector with intact packet-tasked DDoS DLL
samples.marker_line: StormAttack implant: packet DDoS, remote launch and persistence

javascript_evidence: The module calls execFileSync(/usr/bin/osascript, [-e,payload]) at load time. String.raw preserves the full executable AppleScript; it is not a documentation-only string.

The AppleScript impersonates System Preferences, repeatedly collects a hidden answer and validates it using dscl . authonly. The captured login password is not itself written to the uploaded archive in these bytes.

security find-generic-password reads Chrome Safe Storage; its output is staged as storage.txt. Keychain databases, ~/.aws and ~/.ssh are copied into /tmp/osalogging. ditto creates /tmp/osalogging.zip and curl -X PUT --data-binary uploads it to a remote /gate endpoint.

If Trezor Suite is installed, the script downloads a ZIP, overwrites app.asar and Info.plist inside its installed bundle, forces ad-hoc signing and clears extended attributes. Final replacement content was not acquired.

An authorized backup can copy these stores, but the impersonated credential prompt, third-party secret export and wallet resource replacement together establish deceptive credential theft. No legitimate deployment or testing context was supplied.
lookfor_evidence: Version resources claim LookFor 2.0.1.7, Sanny Ltd.; those names and the collector Cryptolocker/Elex label establish no family or legitimate provenance.

Entry 0x40132f calls GUI initialization 0x4038fa. WndProc 0x403153 moves windows off-screen and dispatches reconstruction through WM_COMMAND; it invokes the opaque global pointer at 0x4035a6. 0x40133b performs a 64-KiB backward MZ search and export-table resolution.

0x4011ed reads disjoint pointer/word-length tables, reassembles fragments, and filters dictionary bytes, recovering 3351 bytes. 0x402cd3 applies repeating-key XOR, a message-37 transposition and run expansion. The recovered code manually relocates an embedded loader.

The loader prepares the original PE image by fragment reconstruction, transposition and LZO decompression; it subsequently unmaps/remaps the host image, restores imports and transfers execution. Byte reconstruction stopped before the unmap and did not establish runtime success of the exact packed image.

Recovered original PE: 4096 bytes, SHA-256 717b8b269e7b188d3124a42c1496eb58c905e4790abfc2b1c786f8b7bda73bab, entry 0x401020, valid PE checksum 0x8a01. See decode-lookfor.py and unpack-lookfor.py in scratch for the isolated reconstruction.

The recovered entry reads its own executable and, when not already at the expected temporary path, appends its original wide path to a copied image and launches the temporary copy with SW_HIDE at 0x4011a5. The temporary-instance path derives the appended filename and retries deletion up to 20000 times at 0x4011ea.

0x4011f5 initializes WinINet; it connects to nasap.net:443 and requests /config/8mo.exe. HttpOpenRequestW at 0x401272 receives flags 0x80803000, explicitly ignoring certificate hostname and validity-date failures. InternetReadFile feeds a local executable write at 0x401343; the same filename is used to construct the hidden ShellExecuteW launch path. No working endpoint or final downloaded payload is claimed.

A generic updater could download and launch code. The misleading LookFor wrapper, concealed remapping loader, hidden self-copy/launch, self-removal, unsigned packaging and unchecked remote executable collectively tip the balance to malicious deception. No ransomware, credential theft or specific final family is inferred.
The UTF-16 path corpus starts at unmapped file offset 0x6800; it is not a list of executed drop destinations. No runtime comparison against these sandbox paths was established.
storm_evidence: Outer entry 0x402674 reaches dispatcher 0x401cb0. Configuration DWORD at file 0x4120 equals 3, selecting Active Setup self-copy and StubPath registry registration; alternate branches contain service installation, LanmanServer ServiceDLL replacement and resource-DLL injection. Findings describing code presence do not prove all branches ran.

The resource starts at 0x5060 and contains an intact 39936-byte PE DLL (SHA-256 e58dd623e688da935eb785985f0c55ed8df09bd57567d8a2f6fdc10bf41511e1). Outer 0x401150 selects a child image, creates it, allocates remote memory, writes a DLL path, resolves LoadLibraryA and passes that address and path to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d. Cleanup 0x401390 builds COMSPEC /c del against its own short path.
DLL entry 0x1000741a reaches process-attach code 0x10007176, mutex handling and thread creation at 0x100071c9. The worker checks in with a STORM-formatted report and receives task records.

At 0x10006b45 recv reads a record; a positive result gates copying into the stack dispatch record. Task 5 takes a field of that record and calls 0x100067c2; the helper downloads with URLDownloadToFileA at 0x100068ed and passes the same local destination to CreateProcessA at 0x10006917.

Raw UDP routine 0x1000228e opens AF_INET/SOCK_RAW/IPPROTO_UDP. At 0x10002353 it sends twelve packets per burst, sleeps, and repeats until a shared stop flag changes. Packet handlers also enable SeShutdownPrivilege and call ExitWindowsEx; 0x10006549 is one such shutdown helper.
Host decoding at 0x100063ec XORs with 0x2c then 2; 0x1000634a subtracts 0x64 and XORs with 0x12. The stored host is placeholder a bytes, yielding repeated 0xf9; no usable C2 endpoint is established.

The embedded DLL puts code in a non-executable .data section and retains legacy/malformed loader configuration, so runtime success is uncertain. Concrete remote payload execution, task-driven flooding, persistence and injection code still establish malicious identity. No ransomware, Remcos, WannaCry or DNS reflection claim is made.
changes_and_unsupported_claims: Retain all supported phishing, secret-store copying, wallet substitution, archive upload and StormAttack behaviors. Add carrier scope for AppleScript commands inside JavaScript/TypeScript; restore the validated-phishing finding previously suppressed solely by Keychain targeting.

Move local secret-store copy aggregation from generic credential-file search to collection/file-copy/sensitive; update exact and webroot-loot ancestor consumers. Move local wallet impersonation from supply-chain/trojanized to evasion/masquerade/process/app-substitute without changing its predicates or criticalities.

Move the fragment-loader/path-corpus observation out of sandbox detection into anti-static string junking and set suspicious: its predicates show concealment/path ballast, not a sandbox environment comparison. The matching predicates and scopes are preserved.

Remove concealed-import-user-dir-exe-dropper: a CreateFileA reference plus unused overlay paths never binds a payload write to those paths. Preserve fragment/API concealment and add actual RWX-buffer-call and concealed executable-buffer findings instead. Three supported suspicious concealment findings meet the evidence-supported coverage minimum; no hostile signature is invented for the outer packer.

Rename curl-post-data-binary-file to curl-data-binary-file-body and remove its --data-raw branch. PUT is not POST, and curl --data-raw treats @path literally. Actual binary file-body uploads remain notable; neutral HTTP body observations remain for literal bodies.

Move curl archive/update filename references to fs/path/archive without changing the matcher. Uploads can name archives too; the download composite retains the separate output-option requirement and now explicitly describes co-occurrence.

Add a notable WinINet certificate-ignore rule on the recovered payload, binding the loaded IAT slot to HttpOpenRequestW and the secure/certificate-ignore argument sequence. Altering either the flag mask or the loaded API pointer prevents detection.
consumer_and_fixture_audit: Inspected all exact references and ancestor selectors for the moved credential, wallet, sandbox/dropper, curl archive, upload, executable-memory and archive-creation rules. The web-served credential-loot consumer explicitly retains the moved collection leg. Native sandbox consumers lose unsupported sandbox membership intentionally; Python staging consumers cannot match the PE-only rule. No dependency-specific exception was introduced.

Existing testdata/triage-native-tasking/evidence.txt documents a related LookFor loader but no matching native fixture remains in testdata; an inventory of PE fixtures found no fragment/backscan positive. The reviewed technique was retained, with real loader mutations verifying its separate required legs.

The existing external testdata/hostile/index.applescript.xz fixture retains all six prior hostile findings and every prior suspicious finding, gaining the separately valid phishing observation. Existing renamed-staging, local staging, backup, ordinary-updater and isolated-Keychain controls were tested in standalone and JavaScript-carried forms.

Native controls derive from the actual bytes: remove overlay; change PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE to PAGE_READWRITE; erase only fragment-loop signature; rename declared product/vendor. TLS controls alter the real request mask or IAT pointer, not synthetic stand-in files. Source controls cover PUT, POST, quoted filenames, --data-raw literal @path and @- stdin.

44 assertions across 24 controls pass. Every baseline hostile/suspicious control observation survives, with taxonomy ID mapping, except the two unsupported native claims. The curl --data-raw false file-read match is demonstrated in baseline and absent afterward.
remaining_disagreements: JavaScript remains classifier SUSPICIOUS despite four concrete hostile behaviors; its facts report flow-query-incomplete for cross-language source. This does not invalidate the plainly reachable execFileSync/AppleScript behavior.

Packed downloader changes classifier HOSTILE -> BENIGN after accurate rule correction (fp level 25 -> -1). Cleave does not unpack this custom fragment/remapping chain; only three supported suspicious outer traits fire. Manual recovery proves a hidden remote downloader. This is an engine/classifier coverage gap, not grounds to restore false hostile rules.
StormAttack classifier remains HOSTILE and both outer and embedded-DLL findings are identical before/after.

The unchanged baseline file-create-win matcher still MATCHES the smaller PE, as verified with test-rules. It disappears only from compact emitted output because no firing composite now references the baseline finding. This is engine low-tier stripping, not removal or weakening of the API rule.

Atomscan warns its v18 feature model trails extractor v19. No causal explanation for the classifier misses is asserted. The test-rules inline-YARA detail can say did not match even when its summary and emitted finding say MATCHED; positive and mutated-negative scan outputs independently confirm the new TLS rule.

documentation.supports: 0x1000 ignores certificate hostname, 0x2000 ignores certificate validity dates; 0x800000 enables secure requests.

validation: make validate is the final operation after saved judgments and scans; its completion is reported in the final response.
